best_for: Students, planners and consultants who sketch ideas as mind maps on a desktop and only need the paid tier once they export without a watermark or present often.

points.title: Free works, with a watermark
points.text: The free plan allows up to 10 online maps, 3 sheets per map, 3 days of version history and 5 slides in Pitch mode. Exports carry a watermark and go out as PNG, one map at a time.

points.title: Pro and Premium
points.text: The pricing page lists Pro at USD 4.92 and Premium at USD 8.25 per month, with yearly billing shown by default. Pro removes the watermark and adds PDF, SVG, Markdown and Office export. Premium adds unlimited maps, live collaboration and Gantt editing. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Five computers per subscription
points.text: One Pro or Premium subscription covers up to 5 Mac or PC devices and 5 phones or tablets. There is no perpetual license for individuals; when a plan lapses, your maps stay readable but paid features lock.

points.title: More than one map shape
points.text: Besides classic mind maps it does timelines, matrices and zones, a focus mode called Zen, and Pitch mode to present straight from a map. It can turn Markdown, Word and OPML files into maps.

points.title: Files stay on your disk
points.text: Maps are saved as local files, with cloud sync as an option. That means you can work offline and keep your files in any folder or sync tool you already use.

points.title: Linux trails a few releases
points.text: Linux gets a Flathub build that Flathub marks as verified for XMIND LTD., for x64 and Arm64. It is currently on 26.03 while Windows and macOS are on 27.1.

points.title: Old versions are a Windows thing here
points.text: The Windows installer is per-user (x64 only), and the Windows listing keeps 56 versions. macOS (a universal build for macOS 12 and later) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
